canonicalDecisionBasis._note: Per the brief's own instruction: 'most adopted is a signal, not the answer — the best implementation is the one that already handles the hard cases'. This decision is ordered on that test FIRST, adoption/mandate cited only as corroboration.
canonicalDecisionBasis.hardCaseTest: TypographyControls is the only implementation in this tree offering, on a SINGLE component: (a) responsive tiers (fontSizeTablet/fontSizeMobile via ResponsiveControl reading the ONE global device toggle — confirmed live 2026-08-19, ResponsiveControl.js Spec 35 Phase 1.2, no per-field switcher), (b) theme-token integration (fontSizePresets resolves useSettings('typography.fontSizes') instead of a raw px input), (c) built-in hover-state rows (decoration/transform/weight under a collapsible group) — a hand-rolled font-size control would need to reimplement all three per block it touches.

engineFix._note: A real engine bug was found and fixed while measuring this row, delegated to a background Sonnet agent (dispatch justified: architectural, multi-function, two numeric regression baselines to protect — see /delegate reasoning in the session). Not scoped to typography alone — it generalises for every future control type.
engineFix.bugFound: survey-golden-conformance.js's axisCanonical() did a blanket reached-component check for EVERY control type, reporting VIOLATION for every non-mounting block with zero qualifiesWhen gating — the exact O.16 'phantom backlog' trap. Measured before the fix: typography reported a blanket 67 VIOLATION / 16 CONFORMANT split. Separately, qualifiesFor()'s own-paint check hardcoded colour's CSS regex, so a non-colour type's paintsOwnSurface predicate could never actually match its own declared properties.
engineFix.fixShape: axisCanonical() now calls qualifiesFor() when a block doesn't reach the canonical component, returning MISSING (qualifies) / NOT-APPLICABLE (doesn't) / UNCLEAR instead of blanket VIOLATION — for every type EXCEPT colour, which keeps its pre-existing blanket-VIOLATION path deliberately (colour already gets its own MISSING/NOT-APPLICABLE split from an earlier pre-gate keyed on roster.json surfaces.colour; routing colour through the new qualifiesFor() branch was tested and found to MOVE colour's numbers, so it was excluded to protect the backward-compatibility requirement). qualifiesFor()'s paintsOwnSurface check now reads a new schema field, qualifiesWhen.paintsOwnSurface.cssProperties (a bare array of CSS property name strings — see the border/box-4value/shadow rows below for real usage), building the match regex from it; when a row doesn't declare that field, the function falls back to colour's original hardcoded regex byte-for-byte, so colour's existing measured numbers cannot move even if this fallback path is hit by accident.
engineFix.verified: node run.js --self-test 31-golden-colour-control still reports exactly 408 (unmoved — rule 31 never calls qualifiesFor()/axisCanonical() at all, so this was structurally impossible to break). node scripts/surveys/survey-golden-conformance.js --self-test passes (15/15 fixtures). Colour's canonical-axis distribution diffed row-by-row across all 83 blocks before vs after the fix: 0 differences (CONFORMANT 63 / VIOLATION 2 / NOT-APPLICABLE 6 / MISSING 12, both times).

redesign2026_08_19.rootCause: Confirmed via the real @wordpress/components npm package source (v39.0.0, pulled and read this session — box-control/styles/box-control-styles.ts): BoxControl's InputWrapper/ResetButton/LinkedButtonWrapper are laid out via a CSS grid + HStack combination in WP core's own Emotion-styled internals. No SGS-side CSS targets `.components-box-control` anywhere in this tree (grepped, 0 hits) — this rules out an SGS override as the cause. Patching WP core's internal CSS via scoped override was rejected as the fix (fragile against every WP core update to BoxControl's internals).
redesign2026_08_19.fixShape: New component SgsBoxControl.js (src/components/SgsBoxControl.js) — same data model (a {top,right,bottom,left} box, linked/unlinked toggle, same re-link-collapses-to-one-value behaviour as core's own BoxControl) built from the same native primitives (UnitControl, RangeControl, Button) but hand-laid-out in one Flex row with align="center", so the slider and unlink icon sit exactly level with the input. ResponsiveBoxControl.js now renders SgsBoxControl instead of core's BoxControl (both the showResponsive=false branch and the per-tier ResponsiveControl branch) — ResponsiveBorderRadiusControl / the corner control was UNCHANGED (Bean's complaint was specifically about the padding/margin row, not the radius corners, which use a different core component, __experimentalBorderRadiusControl, not flagged as broken).
redesign2026_08_19.verifiedNotChanged: Same values/onChange(tier,next) contract as before — every one of the 48 blocks already calling ResponsiveBoxControl gets the fix automatically with no call-site changes. Verified via a clean local npx wp-scripts build (isolated worktree, no shared build/ touched).

redesign2026_08_19.colourDualEntry: Border colour is wired to the SAME {name}BorderColour(+Gradient) attribute from TWO mount points in a consuming block's edit.js: (1) a DesignTokenPicker inside the compact 'Border' PanelBody, carrying borderStyle/onBorderStyleChange so its popover includes the style icons, and (2) a row inside SgsColourPanel's list (labelled 'Border colour'), ALSO carrying borderStyle/onBorderStyleChange per Bean's explicit follow-up ('will this popover open when we click the border colour row in the Colour panel?' — yes, both mounts pass the same props). Neither mount owns the attribute; both read/write the same setAttributes call, so there is no sync mechanism to build — React state is the single source of truth already.

canonical._note: CORRECTED 2026-08-19 — the first draft of this row treated contentAlign and textAlign as two separate architectural questions (one resolved, one an open gap). Bean challenged that directly: 'isn't it a variant of the same thing but for text?' Checked against real code (src/blocks/text/edit.js:582-591) and confirmed true — every textAlign implementation found is a FLAT SelectControl with no responsive tiers, while multi-button's contentAlign panel uses ResponsiveOverride (tier-object storage, per-device value). There is no genuine mechanism difference between 'pick a flex-alignment value per tier' and 'pick a text-align value per tier' — both are the SAME pattern (ResponsiveOverride wrapping a SelectControl, tier-object attribute), just with a different option list. One canonical SHAPE now covers both facets.

pattern._noComponentIdentifier: Deliberately NO `component` key here (2026-08-20 audit fix). This is a two-part PATTERN, not one owned component, and neither part is safe to declare alone: (1) ResponsiveOverride resolves as a real file (verified via resolveComponentFiles()) but is used in 23 blocks total (before-after, button, container, cta-section, decorative-image, feature-grid, gallery, google-reviews, hero, media, multi-button, physics-canvas, post-grid, product-search, quote, responsive-logo, separator, site-footer/-row, site-header/-row, trust-bar, trustpilot-reviews) for unrelated tier-object attributes (gap, spacing, etc, not alignment) — declaring it alone would score every one of those 23 as reaching alignment's canonical shape regardless of whether they touch alignment at all, a false-CONFORMANT sweep. (2) SelectControl does NOT resolve via resolveComponentFiles() (it is a bare `@wordpress/components` import, not an SGS-authored file in src/components/) and is mounted raw in 70 blocks for entirely unrelated selects — declaring it would be worse than (1). The prior draft put this description under a `component` key, which the census engine's COMPONENT_IDENTIFIER regex (`^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$`) correctly rejected as prose, so canonicalComponentNames() returned nothing and the axis silently read N/A (83/83) — same as the false-absence pattern this audit was scoped to fix elsewhere, except here the honest answer really is 'no single safely-declarable component', not a fixable oversight. Verdict: leave `canonical` axis at N/A for this type — a fabricated single-identifier declaration would trade an honest N/A for a false CONFORMANT sweep, which is worse.

nativeUi._engineGapNoDetectVia: Deliberately NO `detectVia` field added here (2026-08-20 audit). Verified the family is real — 'typography' is declared in 25 block.json files (python enumeration of src/blocks/*/block.json supports keys, 2026-08-20). But the engine's supportFamilyFromDetectVia() regex (core/golden.js) only captures the FIRST dotted segment after `supports.` and axisNativeUi() only reads ONE level of sub-flags off that family (liveNativeFlags(supports[key])) — it has no way to check a SPECIFIC nested sub-flag like `typography.textAlign` in isolation from typography's other sub-flags (fontSize, lineHeight, fontWeight, textDecoration, etc). Declaring `detectVia: 'block.json supports.typography — any sub-flag set true'` here would fire on ANY typography sub-flag, not textAlign specifically — a false/imprecise VIOLATION any time a block enables e.g. fontSize support for an unrelated reason, and it would silently duplicate typography's own axis (which deliberately declares NO detectVia for exactly this family, per its own row, to avoid the same over-trigger). Proposed engine fix for the main agent, not built here (out of scope, core/golden.js is off-limits this session): a new schema shape, e.g. `nativeUi.detectViaSubFlag: 'typography.textAlign'`, paired with a new evaluator that reads `supports.typography.textAlign === true` specifically rather than the generic any-sub-flag-in-family check `liveNativeFlags()` already does. Until that lands, this axis stays honestly N/A (schema declares no READABLE native-UI competitor) rather than a forced, imprecise measurement.
